description: 2 tactical challenges for White in the Winawer Poisoned Pawn. After 6...Ne7 sidesteps the pin, White strikes with 7.Qg4 — and the pawn on g7 is poisoned.

drills.briefExplanation: 7.Qg4 Qc7 8.Qxg7 Rg8 9.Qxh7 — White collects both kingside pawns while Black scrambles to develop.
drills.description: White to play. Black's 6...Ne7 unpins the knight — play the critical 7.Qg4!, beginning the Poisoned Pawn variation.
drills.explanation: The whole point of the Poisoned Pawn: 7.Qg4 attacks g7, and after 7...Qc7 defending it, 8.Qxg7 Rg8 9.Qxh7 wins a second pawn. Black's compensation is the half-open g-file and pressure on c3 after 9...cxd4. White consolidates with 10.Ne2 (guarding c3, preparing f4) 10...Nbc6 11.f4, keeping the extra material with a playable position.
drills.name: The Poisoned Pawn Grab

drills.briefExplanation: 10.Ne2 Nbc6 11.f4 Bd7 12.Qd3 — centralize the queen, support e5, and get the king to safety.
drills.description: White to play. The pawns are won — now find the consolidation plan after 9...cxd4.
drills.explanation: Grabbing the pawns is only half the variation — keeping them is the rest. 10.Ne2 defends c3 and unblocks f4; after 10...Nbc6 11.f4 the e5 pawn is rock solid and Black's counterplay is stalling. 12.Qd3 centralizes the queen, eyes h7's escape routes, and prepares queenside castling.
drills.name: Consolidating the Loot

name: Winawer Poisoned Pawn — White Tactics
